meta.notes: The dashboard separates first observations, comparable series, company-reported actuals, consensus context, and scenario assumptions. Never infer a trend or expectation gap from a single category.

layers.title: Machine activity
layers.description: Are autonomous systems creating more requests, tool calls, data movement, traces, and machine-to-machine communication?

layers.title: Enterprise adoption & control
layers.description: Are enterprises moving from demos to governed deployments with identity, permissions, observability, and policy controls?

layers.title: Company capture
layers.description: Which public companies convert agentic workload growth into durable revenue, margin, retention, or free-cash-flow improvement?

expectations.theme: Research question — is infrastructure already priced?
expectations.assumption: Test whether market models recognize the second-order request, telemetry, security, and data footprint of agents. Do not presume that they do not.

expectations.theme: Research question — when does control spend monetize?
expectations.assumption: Determine whether identity, data-loss, and agent-permission risk leads to paid control-plane adoption rather than bundled features or deferred spending.
Test whether willingness to pay remains at the application layer while infrastructure is treated as a cost center. This is a live counter-case, not a bearish afterthought.

gaps.evidence: At least three comparable observations across independent lenses
gaps.consensus: No company-level expectation read applies until a macro trend is established

gaps.evidence: Paid adoption, attach, renewal, or price realization—not a product launch alone
Revenue conversion plus margin and cash-return evidence by company
gaps.consensus: At least two point-in-time estimates and a multiple-history view

gaps.evidence: Recurring incidents, policy change, and paid enterprise-control adoption
gaps.consensus: Estimate revisions after validated commercial evidence

breakers.title: Action-oriented activity does not compound
breakers.description: Generic bot traffic can rise while fetcher, tool, or action-oriented share stays flat or falls.
breakers.test: After three comparable observations, action-oriented measures fail to improve while generic AI-bot activity grows.
breakers.downgrade: Do not classify a Wave-2 activity acceleration.

breakers.title: Agents remain assistive, not operational
breakers.description: Usage grows, but humans remain in the loop for every material action and autonomous workflows fail to deepen.
breakers.test: Long-running-task, automation, and enterprise deployment evidence does not improve across new source periods.

breakers.title: AI mediation stays narrow
breakers.description: Models create useful outputs but do not become a material processing layer for routine enterprise events.
breakers.test: Enterprise AI transaction, data-transfer, model-gateway, or workflow evidence stalls outside a small set of use cases.
breakers.downgrade: Treat AI-mediated existing activity as a niche, not a second multiplier.

breakers.title: Hyperscalers internalize the workload
breakers.description: Agentic workloads stay within vertically integrated clouds or model platforms rather than using independent toll roads.
breakers.test: Independent candidates lack usage, attach, or revenue evidence while native cloud services capture the related spend.

breakers.title: Consumption is bundled away
breakers.description: Platforms absorb traffic, logs, and security events into flat-price products, preventing incremental monetization.
breakers.test: Product launches or usage growth occur without disclosed attach, price realization, retention, or revenue acceleration.
breakers.status: Counterevidence present for all core candidates
breakers.downgrade: Do not attribute incremental activity to shareholder capture.

breakers.title: Pricing falls faster than volume rises
breakers.description: AI-related workload grows, but renewal pressure or commodity pricing eliminates revenue leverage.
breakers.test: Traffic or consumption rises while renewal pricing, revenue per unit, or mix deteriorates.
breakers.status: Watch — Akamai delivery pricing pressure is a relevant warning
breakers.downgrade: Use lower revenue-elasticity and valuation assumptions.

breakers.title: Capacity investment destroys cash returns
breakers.description: Network, cloud, and AI capacity spending absorbs the benefit of faster revenue growth.
breakers.test: Capital investment, hosting, co-location, or depreciation rises faster than revenue and cash flow over multiple periods.
breakers.status: Watch — explicit Akamai and cloud-hosting cost warnings
breakers.downgrade: Require a higher cash-return threshold before a capture upgrade.

breakers.title: Enterprises restrict autonomy
breakers.description: Security, legal, identity, or liability concerns keep deployments read-only or tightly limited.
breakers.test: Control products are announced but trusted-action deployments, paid governance adoption, or permission scope do not grow.
breakers.status: Unresolved — product readiness is not deployment evidence
breakers.downgrade: Lengthen time-to-impact assumptions for identity, security, and communication layers.

breakers.title: Infrastructure demand has no moat
breakers.description: Usage rises but the service becomes interchangeable and surplus economics flow to buyers.
breakers.test: Growth is accompanied by falling gross margin, lower NRR, weak RPO, or lack of retention / pricing disclosure.
breakers.downgrade: Do not assign high incremental margins or durable multiples.

breakers.title: The target company misses the mix shift
breakers.description: Wave 2 develops, but economics accrue to a different provider or layer of the stack.
breakers.test: Macro and peer signals improve while the candidate’s relevant KPI, mix, or cash return does not.
breakers.status: Watch — separate theme success from company success
breakers.downgrade: Remove the company from the core queue without rejecting the macro thesis.
